questions.question: Which state of matter has the highest kinetic energy of particles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plasma **has the **highest kinetic energy** of particles compared to other states of matter.
 
• In plasma, particle (ions and free electrons) move at extremely high speeds due to high temperatures, making it the most energetic state.
 
• Plasma is found in environments like **stars** (including the Sun) and **lightning**, where temperatures are very high.
 
• The formation of plasma requires energy input to **ionize gases**, leading to the creation of charged particles.
 
• Unlike gases, plasma consists of charged particles and exhibits unique properties like **electrical conductivity** and **responsiveness to magnetic fields**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinetic Theory of Matter:**

 
 
• This theory explains that particles of matter are always in motion.
 
• The energy of these particles increases with temperature.
 
• It applies to all states of matter - solids, liquids, and gases.
 
 
 
• **Temperature and Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• Kinetic energy of particles is directly proportional to the temperature.
 
• Higher temperatures mean higher kinetic energy and vice versa.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of States of Matter:**
 
 
• Solids have the least kinetic energy due to tightly packed particles.
 
• Liquids have more kinetic energy than solids but less than gases.
 
• Gases have the highest kinetic energy among the three states.
 
 
 
• **Behavior of Gases:**
 
 
• They expand to fill their container.
 
• They are easily compressible due to the large spaces between particles.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of mass and weight of a body, respectively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kg, N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mass** is a fundamental property of matter that quantifies the amount of substance in an object, and its SI unit is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
• **Weight** is the force exerted on a body due to gravity, and its SI unit is the **Newton (N)**.
 
• Weight is calculated as the product of mass and gravitational acceleration (W = mg), where g is approximately 9.81 m/s² on Earth.
 
• The kilogram (kg) is the base unit of mass in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• The Newton (N) is derived from the SI units as 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass vs Weight**:

 
 
• Mass is a scalar quantity and does not change with location, while weight is a vector quantity and changes with the gravitational field strength.
 
• Mass is measured using a balance, while weight is measured using a spring scale.
 
 
 
• **SI Units**:
 
 
• The International System of Units (SI) is the modern form of the metric system and the most widely used system of measurement.
 
• It includes seven base units: meter (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), ampere (A), kelvin (K), mole (mol), and candela (cd).
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Acceleration**:
 
 
• Gravitational acceleration (g) varies slightly over the surface of the Earth, generally taken as 9.81 m/s².
 
• Weight varies slightly depending on altitude and latitude due to variations in gravitational acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• The kilogram was originally defined in 1795 as the mass of one liter of water.
 
• In 2019, the definition of the kilogram was redefined based on the Planck constant, making it more stable and accurate.

questions.question: In what duration will a sum of Rs. 2,100 fetch a simple interest of Rs. 1,050 at 10% per annum rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2,100

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹1,050

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% per annum

**Formula used:**

SI = (P × R × T) / 100

Where, T = Time in years

**Calculations:**

1050 = (2100 × 10 × T) / 100

⇒ 1050 = 210 × T

⇒ T = 1050 / 210

⇒ T = 5 years

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: Magnification produced by a lens is related to the object-distance u, and the image-distance v. This relationship is given by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**v/u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Magnification (M) produced by a lens is defined as the ratio of the image distance (v) to the object distance (u).
 
• The formula for magnification is given by M = v/u, where v is the distance from the lens to the image, and u is the distance from the lens to the object.
 
• This relationship holds true for both convex and concave lenses.
 
• Magnification can also be expressed in terms of the heights of the image (h') and the object (h), M = h'/h.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lens Formula:**

 
 
• The lens formula relates the object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) of a lens: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u.
 
• This formula is applicable to both convex and concave lenses.
 
 
 
• **Types of Lenses:**
 
 
• **Convex Lens:** Converging lens that brings parallel rays of light to a focus.
 
• **Concave Lens:** Diverging lens that spreads parallel rays of light outward.
 
 
 
• **Real and Virtual Images:**
 
 
• **Real Image:** Formed when light rays actually converge and can be projected on a screen; always inverted.
 
• **Virtual Image:** Formed when light rays appear to diverge from a point; cannot be projected on a screen; always upright.
 
 
 
• **Optical Instruments:**
 
 
• Microscopes and telescopes use lenses to magnify objects and provide a closer view.
 
• These instruments utilize the principles of magnification and lens formulas.

questions.question: Ozone shields the surface of the earth from ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun and the amount of ozone in the atmosphere begins to drop sharply due to which of the following synthetic chemicals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorofluorocarbons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are synthetic compounds containing carbon, chlorine, and fluorine.
 
• They are primarily used in refrigeration, air conditioning, and as propellants in aerosol sprays.
 
• CFCs are known to cause the depletion of the ozone layer in the stratosphere.
 
• When CFCs are released into the atmosphere, they rise to the stratosphere where they are broken down by UV radiation, releasing chlorine atoms that destroy ozone molecules.
 
• The use of CFCs has been largely phased out under the Montreal Protocol, an international treaty adopted in 1987 to protect the ozone layer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone Layer**:

 
 
• The ozone layer is a region of Earth's stratosphere that contains a high concentration of ozone (O₃) and absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.
 
• It is crucial for protecting living organisms on Earth from UV radiation, which can cause skin cancer, cataracts, and other health issues.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol**:
 
 
• The Montreal Protocol is an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of numerous substances, including CFCs, that are responsible for ozone depletion.
 
• It was agreed upon on September 16, 1987, and has been ratified by 198 countries, making it one of the most successful environmental agreements.
 
 
 
• **Ultraviolet (UV) Radiation**:
 
 
• UV radiation is a type of electromagnetic radiation that comes from the Sun and is invisible to the human eye.
 
• It is divided into three types based on wavelength: UVA, UVB, and UVC, with UVB being the most harmful to the skin and DNA.
 
 
 
• **Alternatives to CFCs**:
 
 
• Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) and hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) are alternatives to CFCs that do not deplete the ozone layer.
 
• However, HFCs are potent greenhouse gases and contribute to global warming, leading to the development of more sustainable alternatives like hydrofluoroolefins (HFOs).

questions.question: A current of 2 A is flowing through a conductor of resistance 12 Ω. Then the potential difference across the conductor is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The potential difference (V) across a conductor can be calculated using Ohm's Law: V = I × R, where I is the current and R is the resistance.
 
• Given a current (I) of 2 A and a resistance (R) of 12 Ω, the potential difference (V) is calculated as V = 2 A × 12 Ω = 24 V.
 
• Option 2, which states 24 V, is the correct answer.
 
• Ohm's Law is fundamental in understanding the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in electrical circuits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law**: Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• **Resistance (R)**: Resistance is a measure of the opposition to the flow of current in an electrical circuit, measured in ohms (Ω).
 
• **Current (I)**: Current is the rate of flow of electric charge in a circuit, measured in amperes (A).
 
• **Voltage (V)**: Voltage is the electrical potential difference between two points in a circuit, measured in volts (V).
 
• **Applications**: Understanding these concepts is crucial for designing and analyzing electrical circuits used in various applications, from household wiring to complex industrial systems.

questions.question: In what direction is fluid pressure transmitted in any confined mass of fluid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Undiminished in all directions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Pascal's Law, fluid pressure is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions in a confined fluid.
 
• This principle applies to fluids at rest, ensuring the pressure at any point in the fluid is the same in every direction.
 
• Pascal's Law is fundamental in hydraulic systems where pressure applied at one point is transmitted to another point using an incompressible fluid.
 
• Examples of applications include hydraulic presses, car brakes, and hydraulic jacks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pascal's Law:**

 
 
• Formulated by Blaise Pascal, a French mathematician, physicist, and inventor.
 
• States that a change in pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to all portions of the fluid and to the walls of its container.
 
 
 
• **Hydraulic Systems:**
 
 
• Utilize Pascal's Law to multiply force by using fluid pressure.
 
• Commonly found in machinery like excavators, hydraulic presses, and braking systems.
 
 
 
• **Pressure in Fluids:**
 
 
• Pressure is defined as force per unit area and is measured in Pascals (Pa) or atmospheres (atm).
 
• In fluids, pressure increases with depth due to the weight of the fluid above.
 
 
 
• **Incompressible Fluids:**
 
 
• Fluids that do not change in volume when pressure is applied, ideal for hydraulic systems.
 
• Examples include liquids like water and oil.

Circumference of the circle = 2πr

Time taken (t) = 2 seconds

Speed (v) = (2πr) / 2

⇒ v = πr metre/second

questions.question: In an aqueous solution, acid and base produce:

options.text: Li⁺ ions and CO₃²⁻ ions, respectively
Na⁺ ions and CO₃²⁻ ions, respectively
H⁺ ions and OH⁻ ions, respectively

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**H+ ions and OH- ions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In an aqueous solution, acids release **H+ ions (hydrogen ions)**, which are responsible for the acidic properties of the solution.
 
• Bases, on the other hand, release **OH- ions (hydroxide ions)** in an aqueous solution, which are responsible for the basic properties.
 
• The interaction of H+ ions from acids and OH- ions from bases leads to the formation of water (H₂O) and is termed as a neutralization reaction.
 
• This phenomenon is fundamental to the concept of pH, which measures the acidity or basicity of a solution.
 
• According to the Brønsted-Lowry theory, acids are proton donors (H+), and bases are proton acceptors (OH-).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **pH Scale:**

 
 
• The pH scale ranges from 0 to 14, with 7 being neutral.
 
• A pH less than 7 indicates an acidic solution, while a pH greater than 7 indicates a basic solution.
 
• The pH scale is logarithmic, meaning each whole number change represents a tenfold change in H+ ion concentration.
 
 
 
• **Strong vs. Weak Acids and Bases:**
 
 
• Strong acids and bases dissociate completely in water, releasing more H+ or OH- ions, respectively.
 
• Weak acids and bases partially dissociate in water, releasing fewer H+ or OH- ions.
 
 
 
• **Neutralization Reaction:**
 
 
• This is a chemical reaction in which an acid and a base react to form water and a salt.
 
• The general equation for a neutralization reaction is: Acid + Base → Salt + Water.
 
• Neutralization reactions are exothermic, releasing heat.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Acids and Bases:**
 
 
• Acids are used in various industries, including food preservation, cleaning agents, and chemical manufacturing.
 
• Bases find applications in soap making, cleaning products, and as antacids in medicine.

questions.question: A cistern is filled by Pipe A and Pipe B together in 2.4 hours. Pipe A alone can fill the cistern at the rate of 100 litres per hour. Pipe B alone can fill the cistern in 4 hours. What is the capacity of the cistern?

Let total work be the LCM of 2.4 and 4 = 12 units.

Efficiency of B = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 units/hr.

Efficiency of A = 5 − 3 = 2 units/hr ⇒ Time for A = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 hours.

Total capacity = Time × Filling rate = 6 × 100 = 600 litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 600 litres.**

questions.question: The work done by a person pushing a brick parallel to the ground with a force of 2 N is 3 J. The displacement caused by the force is equal to ______

• Work is defined as the **product of the force applied** and the **displacement caused** in the direction of the force.
 
• The formula for work is: **W = F × d**, where **W** is the work done, **F** is the force applied, and **d** is the displacement.
 
• In this problem, the given values are:
 
 
• **Work (W) = 3 J**
 
• **Force (F) = 2 N**
 
 
 
• To find the displacement, rearrange the formula: **d = W / F**.
 
• Substituting the given values:

• Thus, the **displacement** caused by the force is **1.5 meters**.
 
• The correct option is **Option 2**__, which corresponds to **1.5 m**.

• **Displacement**__

questions.question: In the electrolytic refining process of metals, electrolyte is made up of which of the following?

• In the electrolytic refining process, the **electrolyte** used is a solution of **metal salt**.
 
• This solution contains ions of the metal that is being refined.
 
• The impure metal is made the anode, and a thin sheet of pure metal acts as the cathode.

• **Anode Mud:**
 
 
• The residue left behind at the anode during electrolytic refining is known as anode mud.
 
• Anode mud can contain precious metals like gold and silver, which can be recovered separately.
 
 
 
• **Cathode and Anode:**
 
 
• The cathode is the electrode where reduction (gain of electrons) takes place.
 
• The anode is the electrode where oxidation (loss of electrons) occurs.
 
 
 
• **Electrolyte:**
 
 
• The electrolyte is a conducting solution that allows the flow of ions during electrolysis.

• Binary fission is a type of asexual reproduction commonly found in prokaryotes such as bacteria.
 
• In binary fission, a single organism divides into two parts, each of which develops into a new individual.
 
• This process results in the formation of two genetically identical daughter cells.
 
• Binary fission involves the replication of the parent organism's DNA followed by the division of the cytoplasm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Prokaryotes are unicellular organisms that lack a nucleus, such as bacteria.
 
• Eukaryotes have a defined nucleus and include organisms such as plants, animals, and fungi.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis:**
 
 
• A type of cell division that occurs in eukaryotic cells, resulting in two genetically identical daughter cells.

• **Cell Cycle:**
 
 
• Consists of stages G1, S, G2, and M phase (mitosis) in eukaryotic cells.

questions.question: Some seeds are dispersed when the fruits burst with sudden jerks and the seeds are scattered far from the parent plant. This happens in fruits of which of the following plants?

• This method of seed dispersal is known as **explosive or ballistic dispersal**.
 
• In **Castor** (Ricinus communis), the fruits dry out and split open forcefully to scatter seeds.

• **Explosive Mechanism**
 
 
• Plants like Castor and Balsam exhibit an explosive mechanism where the fruit dehisces (splits open) suddenly to release seeds.
 
• This mechanism involves the buildup of tension in the fruit's tissues, which is released suddenly to scatter seeds.
 
 
 
• **Other Plants with Explosive Dispersal**
 
 
• Other plants that use explosive seed dispersal include Touch-Me-Not (Mimosa pudica) and Pea family members like Lupins.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Explosive Dispersal**
 
 
• Reduces competition for resources among seedlings.
 
• Helps in the colonization of new areas.
 
• Ensures genetic diversity by spreading seeds over a wider area.

questions.question: A student has an eye-power of -0.5D. What is the focal length and type of lens of spectacles that she should use for correcting this defect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-2.0 m, concave lens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The focal length of a lens is given by the inverse of the power of the lens (f = 1/P).
 
• Given the eye power of -0.5D, the focal length (f) = 1/(-0.5) = -2.0 m.
 
• A negative power indicates that the lens is concave, which is used to correct myopia (nearsightedness).
 
• Concave lenses are diverging lenses, meaning they spread out light rays that have been refracted through them.
 
• The student should therefore use a concave lens with a focal length of -2.0 meters to correct her vision defect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Myopia (Nearsightedness)**

 
 
• Myopia is a common vision condition where close objects are seen clearly, but distant objects appear blurry.
 
• It occurs when the eyeball is too long or the cornea is too curved, causing light rays to focus in front of the retina.
 
 
 
• **Concave Lenses**
 
 
• Concave lenses are thinner at the center than at the edges.
 
• They cause parallel rays of light to diverge, spreading out from a point.
 
 
 
• **Lens Power**
 
 
• The power of a lens is measured in diopters (D), which is the reciprocal of the focal length in meters (P = 1/f).
 
• Negative power indicates a concave lens, while positive power indicates a convex lens.
 
 
 
• **Corrective Lenses**
 
 
• Corrective lenses are designed to bend light rays to compensate for the refractive errors of the eye.
 
• They help focus light directly on the retina, providing clear vision.

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 20 and 24 minutes, respectively, and a waste pipe can empty 3 gallons per minute. All the three pipes working together can fill the tank in 15 minutes. The capacity of the tank is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Two pipes can fill a tank in 20 and 24 minutes respectively and a waste pipe can empty 3 gallons per minute. 

 All three pipes working together can fill the tank in 15 minutes. 

Formula used:

Capacity = Time × Efficiency

Calculation:

Let total capacity = LCM[20, 24, 15] = 120 units

E(1st Pipe) = 120/20 = 6

E(2nd Pipe) = 120/24 = 5 

E(All three Pipes) = 120/15= 8 [∵ Capacity = Time × Efficiency]

3rd Pipe = E(All three Pipes) - E(1st Pipe) - E(2nd Pipe)

⇒ 3rd Pipe = 8 - 6 - 5 = - 3 units 

[negative as 3rd Pipe is a waste pipe]

∴ 3rd Pipe empties 3 units every minute

According to the question,

3 units = 3 gallons.

Thus, Capacity of tank = (120/3) × 3 = 120 gallons

∴ Capacity of the tank is 120 gallons.

• When a soft iron bar is introduced inside a current-carrying solenoid, the magnetic field inside the solenoid increases significantly.
 
• Soft iron has high magnetic permeability, which means it enhances the magnetic field by becoming magnetized itself.
 
• The magnetic domains in the soft iron align with the magnetic field created by the solenoid, thus amplifying the overall magnetic field.

• Materials with high magnetic permeability, like soft iron, are used to enhance magnetic fields in various applications.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnet:**
 
 
• An electromagnet is formed by passing an electric current through a coil of wire wrapped around a magnetic core (usually soft iron).
 
• The current generates a magnetic field, which magnetizes the core, thus creating a strong magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Solenoid:**

__
 
• **Roots** exhibit **positive geotropism**, meaning they grow in the direction of gravitational pull, which is downwards.
 
• This downward growth of roots helps in **anchoring the plant** firmly in the soil.
 
• The primary role of roots is to **absorb water and nutrients** from the soil, which is essential for the plant's survival and growth.

• It is a growth response to gravity observed in plants.
 
• Roots show positive geotropism (growth towards gravity), while shoots show negative geotropism (growth away from gravity).
 
 
 
• **Root System Types**:
 
 
• **Taproot system**: A single main root grows downwards with smaller lateral roots (e.g., carrot).
 
• **Fibrous root system**: Many small roots spread out from the base of the stem (e.g., grass).
 
 
 
• **Root Functions**:

questions.question: A bus travel the first 60 m in 30 s and then another 80 m in 40 s. Calculate the average speed of the bus in m s⁻¹.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed is calculated as the ratio of total distance covered to the total time taken.

Total Distance = 60 + 80 = 140 m

Total Time = 30 + 40 = 70 s

Average Speed = 140 ÷ 70 = 2 m s⁻¹

**∴ The correct answer is 2 m s⁻¹.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First distance (d₁) = 60 m

First time (t₁) = 30 s

Second distance (d₂) = 80 m

Second time (t₂) = 40 s

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total Distance = d₁ + d₂

⇒ Total Distance = 60 + 80 = 140 m

⇒ Total Time = t₁ + t₂

⇒ Total Time = 30 + 40 = 70 s

⇒ Average Speed = 140 ÷ 70

⇒ Average Speed = 2 m s⁻¹

**∴ The correct answer is 2 m s⁻¹.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When a journey is divided into equal distances covered at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by the formula (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a journey involves travelling at speeds x and y for exactly equal time intervals, the overall average speed is simply the arithmetic mean: (x + y) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds. For objects moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds.

questions.question: Which of the following is the dispersed phase of automobile exhaust?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Solid phase**__.

__
 
• Automobile exhaust consists of various components in different phases, including solid, liquid, and gaseous phases.
 
• The dispersed phase in automobile exhaust is primarily the solid phase.
 
• Particulate matter (PM), which includes soot, metals, and other solid particles, constitutes the solid phase of automobile exhaust.
 
• These solid particles are a major concern due to their adverse health effects, including respiratory and cardiovascular diseases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It includes PM10 (particles with diameters of 10 micrometers or smaller) and PM2.5 (particles with diameters of 2.5 micrometers or smaller).
 
 
 
• **Health Effects:**
 
 
• Exposure to particulate matter can lead to serious health problems, including asthma, lung cancer, and heart disease.
 
• Children, elderly, and individuals with pre-existing health conditions are particularly vulnerable to the effects of particulate matter.
 
 
 
• **Sources of Particulate Matter:**
 
 
• Common sources include vehicle emissions, industrial processes, construction activities, and natural sources like wildfires and volcanic eruptions.
 
 
 
• **Regulations:**
 
 
• Governments and environmental agencies worldwide have set standards to limit emissions of particulate matter to protect public health and the environment.
 
• In many countries, vehicles are required to meet specific emission standards that limit the amount of particulate matter they can emit.

questions.question: The ratio of milk to water in 10 litres of a mixture is 3:2. The quantity of milk in the mixture will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of milk to water in 10 litres of a mixture is 3:2.

**Formula used:**

Milk quantity = (Total mixture × Milk ratio) / (Milk ratio + Water ratio)

**Calculations:**

Total mixture = 10 litres

Milk ratio = 3

Water ratio = 2

⇒ Milk quantity = (10 × 3) / (3 + 2)

⇒ Milk quantity = 30 / 5

⇒ Milk quantity = 6 litres

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: While dissolving solute in a solution, when no more solute can be dissolved in a solution at a given temperature, it is called _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a saturated solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A saturated solution is one in which no more solute can be dissolved at a given temperature.
 
• In a saturated solution, the concentration of solute remains constant as long as the temperature and pressure remain unchanged.
 
• When a solution reaches saturation, any additional solute will remain undissolved and will form a precipitate.
 
• Saturation is a dynamic equilibrium between the dissolved solute and the undissolved solute.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Colloidal Solution**:

 
 
• A colloidal solution contains particles that are intermediate in size between those in solutions and suspensions.
 
• These particles do not settle out and cannot be separated by ordinary filtering.
 
 
 
• **Suspension**:
 
 
• A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture in which the solute particles do not dissolve but remain dispersed throughout the bulk of the medium.
 
• The particles in a suspension are larger than those in solutions and colloids and can be separated by filtration.
 
 
 
• **Unsaturated Solution**:
 
 
• An unsaturated solution is one that contains less solute than the maximum amount that can be dissolved at a given temperature.
 
• More solute can be dissolved in an unsaturated solution until it becomes saturated.
 
 
 
• **Supersaturated Solution**:
 
 
• A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than it would under normal circumstances.
 
• It is formed by cooling a saturated solution, causing the excess solute to remain in solution.
 
• Supersaturated solutions are unstable and can precipitate the excess solute upon disturbance.

questions.question: Consider an object moving along a straight line, it starts from point A, reaches point B. and then returns to point A. If the distance between A and B is 20 m, then the net displacement of the object is:

Displacement refers to the straight-line distance between the initial and final positions of the object, along with the direction. It doesn't depend on the path taken by the object.

• The initial position and the final position are the same (point A), so the displacement is zero.

Thus, despite the object traveling 40 meters in total (20 meters each way), the **net displacement** is 0 meters, because its initial and final positions coincide.

 
• 
 Net Displacement = Final Position - Initial Position

questions.question: If the magnitude of the force exerted by the earth on the moon is 2.02 x 10²⁰ N, then the magnitude of the force exerted by the moon on the earth is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2) 2.02 × 10²⁰ N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to **Newton's Third Law of Motion**, every action has an equal and opposite reaction, meaning the force exerted by the moon on the earth is equal in magnitude to the force exerted by the earth on the moon.
 
• The magnitude of the force between the earth and the moon is governed by **Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation**.
 
• The force of attraction depends on the masses of the earth and moon and the distance between them, but the magnitude is identical for both bodies.
 
• Since the force exerted by the earth on the moon is given as **2.02 × 10²⁰ N**, the force exerted by the moon on the earth is also **2.02 × 10²⁰ N**.
 
• This mutual force ensures the moon remains in orbit around the earth, demonstrating gravitational interaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton’s Third Law of Motion:**

 
 
• States that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• The forces are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction.
 
 
 
• **Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation:**
 
 
• States that every particle attracts every other particle in the universe with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• The formula is: F = G × (m₁ × m₂) / r², where G is the gravitational constant.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Constant (G):**
 
 
• The value of G is approximately 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N(m²/kg²).
 
• It is a fundamental constant used in the calculation of gravitational forces.
 
 
 
• **Earth-Moon System:**
 
 
• The moon orbits the earth due to the gravitational force exerted by the earth.
 
• The mutual gravitational force ensures stability in the earth-moon system.
 
• The average distance between the earth and the moon is approximately 384,400 km.

questions.question: Which is/are present at the growing tips of stems and roots and increase(s) the length of the stem and the root?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only apical meristem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The apical meristem is a region of actively dividing cells found at the tips of stems and roots in plants.
 
• This meristem is responsible for the primary growth of the plant, increasing its length.
 
• The cells in the apical meristem are undifferentiated, allowing them to continuously divide and contribute to new tissue formation.
 
• Apical meristems are crucial for the elongation of the plant, enabling it to grow taller and roots to penetrate deeper into the soil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meristematic Tissue:**

 
 
• Meristematic tissues are regions in plants where cells remain in a continuous state of division.
 
• They are classified into apical, lateral, and intercalary meristems based on their location and function.
 
 
 
• **Lateral Meristem:**
 
 
• Lateral meristems, such as the vascular cambium and cork cambium, contribute to the secondary growth, increasing the girth of the plant.
 
 
 
• **Intercalary Meristem:**
 
 
• Intercalary meristems are found at the base of nodes and leaf blades, contributing to the regrowth of grass stems after cutting.
 
 
 
• **Primary vs. Secondary Growth:**
 
 
• Primary growth refers to the vertical elongation of the plant, while secondary growth refers to the thickening of the plant body.

__
 
• Adrenaline, also known as epinephrine, is a hormone released by the adrenal glands in response to stress or excitement.
 
• It prepares the body for 'fight-or-flight' response, causing several physiological changes.
 
• **Heart beats faster:** Adrenaline increases the heart rate to pump more blood to muscles and vital organs.
 
• **Breathing rate increases:** It also increases the respiratory rate to supply more oxygen to the body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blood Pressure:** Adrenaline typically increases blood pressure by causing the blood vessels to constrict, not decrease it.
 
• **Sympathetic Nervous System:** Adrenaline is part of the body's sympathetic nervous system, which is responsible for the 'fight-or-flight' response.
 
• **Glucose Levels:** It also increases glucose levels in the blood by stimulating glucose release from the liver.
 
• **Adrenal Glands:** These glands are located on top of the kidneys and are responsible for the production of several important hormones including adrenaline.
 
• **Medical Use:** Adrenaline is used medically in emergencies like cardiac arrest, anaphylaxis, and severe asthma attacks.
